data.narrative:
ElectroFlow Technologies is a Seed-stage company in the Climate & Energy sector founded by Eric McShane and Evan Gardner. The valuation analysis draws on a comparables universe of 8 private peers and 1 public company (LNZA) operating in climate and energy. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tier positioning to support a robust peer-median approach.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation technique here. Using the company's $10M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied value of $25M. This method captures the expected value accretion expected between funding rounds for companies at this stage.

Given the single applicable methodology, the analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, with a median of $25M. Key uncertainties stem from the absence of narrow-filter comparable data—no peer companies at identical stage and valuation tier were available for cross-validation. This constraint limits confidence in the range width. Any refined valuation would benefit from either (1) identification of additional Climate & Energy seed-stage comparables or (2) forward-looking financial metrics specific to ElectroFlow's technology and commercial traction that might anchor alternative approaches.
